titre: How the Dossier checks the four reports.
lede: This page shows what the Dossier is made of: which reports it reads, which five controls it runs on each, what its own public measure covers, and where it does not guess. The Dossier is the audit piece of the suite: it proves the chain, or it names what is missing.

sections.h2: Five controls, run in order, refusals named
html: Each report the Dossier reads passes the same five controls: present (a readable report from a named tool), sealed (the content hash it carries is the content hash of its content), signed (the public record it cites carries the tool's signature), fresh (measured within the declared rhythm; due under two rhythms, stale beyond), consistent (one dataset, one seal; an unknown tool version is named and not guessed). The registry derives the list from code: an absent control is computed, never recited.
Each verdict carries its reason in words. A report that cannot state its measurement day is not called stale: it is named as unjudgeable, which is a different and worse fact, and the Dossier says it.

verif.p: The suite exercises each control in both directions, refusals included.

cmd.n: the five controls and their refusals, with the rest of the suite

sections.h2: Its own public measure: the suite, judged by the Dossier
html: The Dossier's public record is the suite judging itself: it runs on the public records of the other tools and prints coverage, seals, signatures and freshness as it finds them on the day of the measure. On day one that meant three questions of four covered with the fourth named missing, two seals recomputed, and zero verifiable signatures, printed and not waved through. A Dossier that flattered its own suite would be worthless to a reviewer.

verif.p: The public record is sealed; recompute the content hash with the repository's own tool.

cmd.n: says: already sealed, and the seal matches

sections.h2: The rhythm is declared, and age is counted against it
html: Freshness only means something against a rhythm, and the rhythm is yours: ninety days by default, named in the record as a declaration, changed with a flag an auditor can see. The record photographs the settings it was measured under, so two Dossiers can be compared knowing whether the rule moved between them.

verif.p: The record carries its settings block, rhythm included.

cmd.c: python3 -c "import json; r=json.load(open('releve-public.json'))['reglages']; print(r['rythmeJours'], 'days, stale beyond', r['staleApres'], 'rhythms')"
cmd.n: prints the declared rhythm the verdicts were judged under
